title: Applicability,rights and remedy boundaries
question: How can applicability be justified without inventing a waiver or misapplying a specialized legal instrument?
contribution: An applicability disposition must retain its authority,rationale and scope rather than acting as a fourth gate state. A gross/serious-violations remedy text offers limited analogies about dignity,privacy and non-repetition,but its legal scope cannot be imported wholesale into ordinary project governance.
limits: Toy non-waivable4.1/4.11 are assumptions,not an owner decision;all eleven overarching commitments remain under owner review. No real remedy or affected-party assessment performed.

title: Provenance and downstream evidence invalidation
question: What changes when support is revised,invalidated or only structurally consistent?
contribution: Versioned evidence and provenance-of-provenance motivate tracing dependency impacts. Consistency of recorded history does not establish factual truth. An invalidated support should reopen affected conclusions;it does not automatically prove them false.
limits: Only retrieved overviews/rationale read;no fullPROVconformance. Dependency DAG is a toy application restriction,not a claim that every provenance relation must be acyclic.

title: Reviewer independence,roles and disclosed conflicts
question: Can different names conceal the conflicts or insufficient competence that matter to review?
contribution: The distinction between author,reviewer and owner must be recorded along with qualifications and declared conflicts. Source discussion of institutional oversight warns against treating a name check as independence. NISTpermits contextual assessment;the two-reviewer toy is not attributed to NISTas universal.
limits: No real identities,qualifications,organizational conflicts or independent reviewer assessed. Search excerpts do not substitute for unread control bodies.

title: Scoped delegation and least privilege
question: How can delegated capabilities remain inside parent scope rather than amplify it?
contribution: A provenance description of delegation is not authorization. A proposed capability model separately bounds actor,resource,action,purpose,version andexpiry,and rejects childgrants wider than parentgrants.
limits: No signature or issuer-authenticity test,no deployment,no claim ofNISTcontrol implementation. Empty grants can validate structurally but authorize no action.

title: Authorization changes between check and use
question: Can cached approval survive a scope,version,time or basis change before the modeled action?
contribution: A current-use check is a different predicate from a historical permission check. The new toy separates CHECKfromCOMMITand includes real executable stale-cache counterexamples,not just predicted fixed outputs.
limits: Sequential interleavings,horizon5,not a real distributed-concurrency/latency test;clock,updates and enforcement are idealized. Sole-basis withdrawal is not a universal deletion doctrine.

title: Integrated assurance,negative findings and proportionality
question: Which conclusions can the evidence actually support,and what remains unknown after more cycles?
contribution: Combine source/version/rights/review/authority evidence without allowing missing review or projected benefits to be offset by scores. Execute intentionally unsafe alternative policies and preserve examples. Broader effectiveness remains an empirical question.
limits: Same author produces specifications,oracles and reproduction. No independent review,legal certification,source authenticity proof,field validation or complete global mapping.
